topic: Characterize the adaptive minimax number N*(n,K,d,tau,s) of size-at-most-s stochastic hard interventions needed to recover the oriented union of true edges across K DAG components with union indegree at most d and mixture-ancestor cyclic complexity at most tau. A query returns the complete barred-copy d-separation relation in the I-mixture DAG, with the observational oracle free and I-mixture faithfulness as the population bridge. Derive an explicit universal-factor frontier over every feasible s, legal full-oracle transcript lower pairs, and exact formulas for directed-tree mixtures and the cycle-free-ancestor class. Upper bounds must exploit emergent-path parent blocking, not merely replay CADIM or an unevaluated decision-tree recursion. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For Delta=V, the complete CI oracle reduces to surviving descendant sets of targeted roots; 15,600 exhaustive three-node and 76,800 randomized four-node CI checks found no discrepancy. Degree-preserving parent-swap adversaries support feasibility thresholds s=d for cycle-free ancestors and s=min(d+1,n-1) once cyclic complexity one is allowed. Exact supported slices are N*=3 for three-node two-tree mixtures at s>=2, N*=n for cycle-free indegree-one mixtures at s=1, and N*=n at the dense endpoint; twelve positive-rational fixtures passed 6,272 exact probability CI checks. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove matching all-parameter adaptive count bounds by making enough blocker requirements coexist on a legal baseline transcript, or show how adaptation exploits their incompatibility, and complete the arbitrary-tree/cycle-free formulas. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently exhaust the four-node K=2,d<=2,tau<=1,Delta=V full barred-copy oracle, starting with the d=2 parent-swap pair, over every size-two target and conditioning set; any distinguishing answer or failure of simultaneous faithful rational realization stops or pivots the run. open_problems.open_problem: Determine the adaptive minimax intervention-count frontier N*(n,K,d,tau,s), up to universal constants for every feasible size cap s, for recovering the oriented union of true edges from a free observational oracle and complete I-mixture conditional-independence oracles.

source_refs.claim: CADIM uses O(n^2) interventions, while lower bounds on the number of constrained-size interventions are explicitly left for future work.
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Dmitriy A. Katz, Dennis Wei, Prasanna Sattigeri, and Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: For a single DAG, bounded-size intervention counts admit separating-system constructions and lower bounds that remain valid against deterministic adaptive algorithms on complete skeletons.
source_refs.author: Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Murat Kocaoglu, Alexandros G. Dimakis, and Sriram Vishwanath

source_refs.claim: Single-DAG search with bounded-size interventions is controlled within logarithmic factors by a graph-specific verification number based on covered-edge separation.
source_refs.author: Davin Choo, Kirankumar Shiragur, and Arnab Bhattacharyya

open_problems.why_unsolved: Varıcı et al. determine worst-case intervention size for a local mixture-parent query and give an O(n^2)-intervention recovery algorithm, but explicitly leave constrained-size intervention-count lower bounds open. Single-DAG count arguments begin with a known observational MEC and charge interventions for separating or orienting edges in chordal chain components. A mixture may instead have an unknown union skeleton, observationally inseparable nonedges, and cross-component ancestor cycles. Thus a separating-system or verification-number adversary is not automatically legal: all blocker requirements must coexist in two valid K-DAG mixtures producing the same complete barred-copy d-separation transcript along an adaptive baseline. Conversely, a matching upper bound must amortize how targeting a source and blocking emergent paths resolves several union-edge alternatives at once.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Explicit functions L(n,K,d,tau,s) and U(n,K,d,tau,s) with L <= N* <= U and U/L universally bounded, including the exact infeasible regime, legal full-oracle indistinguishable pairs proving L, and an adaptive emergent-path-blocking policy attaining U.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly separates maximum intervention size from total intervention count and explicitly identifies the missing constrained-size count lower bound.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Mixtures create inseparable emergent pairs and cross-component cycles -> interventions are needed for both skeleton and orientation recovery -> locally size-optimal tests plus an O(n^2) algorithm do not determine the minimax count -> characterize N*(n,K,d,tau,s).

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the separating-system adversary and information-theoretic lower-bound proof, replacing endpoint separation by simultaneous mixture blocker requirements.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest all-size-cap intervention-count theorem, including adaptive lower bounds; the first step that changes is constructing a legal mixture transcript rather than selecting a total order on a complete single-DAG skeleton.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the covered-edge verification-number characterization and graph-separator search proof to unresolved true-edge-versus-emergent alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired frontier likewise needs a lower benchmark and an adaptive policy charged against it, but the mixture benchmark must range over full oracle-equivalent alternatives rather than covered reversals inside one MEC.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt allocation matching and confidence-based track-and-stop analysis to finite samples from interventions selected by the population-oracle design.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Candidate mixture unions can be treated as competing causal structures indexed by the separating interventions, yielding a natural fixed-confidence estimation rung after the oracle-count theorem.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive exact closed-form adaptive intervention counts across every feasible size cap for K-component directed-tree mixtures and for mixtures whose union ancestor relation is cycle-free.

source_refs.claim: For directed-tree mixtures the worst-case local intervention size is K+1, and for cycle-free mixture ancestors CADIM's maximum intervention size is optimal, but its total count remains O(n^2).
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Dmitriy A. Katz, Dennis Wei, Prasanna Sattigeri, and Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: For one causal tree, a central-node adaptive policy is within factor two of the minimum intervention count, while information-greedy selection can be exponentially suboptimal.
source_refs.author: Kristjan Greenewald, Dmitriy Katz, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Sara Magliacane, Murat Kocaoglu, Enric Boix-Adserà, and Guy Bresler

source_refs.claim: For a known single-DAG skeleton, limited-intervention design is polynomial-time solvable when the skeleton is a tree or clique tree.
source_refs.author: Murat Kocaoglu, Alexandros G. Dimakis, and Sriram Vishwanath

open_problems.why_unsolved: The existing mixture-tree result controls how many nodes one local test must target, not how many adaptive tests recover the entire oriented union. The single-tree centroid argument assumes a known undirected tree and that an intervention localizes one unknown root. In a mixture, the union need not be a tree, and an oracle answer aggregates K descendant systems plus emergent paths. Its progress lemma must therefore be replaced by a theorem that a target with parent blockers removes a quantified fraction of all still-legal mixture alternatives. The literature contains the 2024 local mixture result and single-tree intervention policies, but no exact total-count formula for arbitrary directed-tree mixtures or the cycle-free-ancestor class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise exact formula for N* on directed-tree mixtures and on the cycle-free-ancestor class as a function of n,K,d,s, proved by an explicit adaptive blocker or centroid policy and matching full-oracle transcript adversaries.

writing_exemplar.why: Its tree theorem and cyclic-complexity narrative provide the precise scope boundary that the count formulas would complete.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Tree components sharply reduce local blocker size -> cycle-free mixture ancestors remove the cyclic size penalty -> CADIM still spends quadratically many interventions without a matching count law -> obtain exact adaptive counts for these structured classes.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the Delta-through-path characterization and the intervention formed from the queried source plus relevant child or parent blockers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the load-bearing local identification argument for the destination model; an exact count theorem must amortize those blockers across many candidate pairs.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the central-node intervention rule and its constant-factor progress proof, using a potential on unresolved mixture alternatives rather than posterior mass over one root.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems exploit tree-induced uniqueness of paths for adaptive savings; the destination proof must handle K simultaneous paths and a generally non-tree union.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over its finite-interventional-sample Bayesian updating and recovery analysis, with likelihoods indexed by candidate mixture unions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the nearest finite-sample recovery machinery for a tree-structured adaptive intervention problem and supplies an estimation rung after the population formula.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize size-s interventional oracle equivalence for K-tuples of DAGs by giving necessary and sufficient graphical conditions for identical complete barred-copy d-separation relations under every intervention of size at most s, and identify exactly which union-edge orientations are invariant within each class.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives local edge-identifiability conditions and examples of different component partitions that agree under all intervention sets, but no global mixture interventional-equivalence characterization.
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Dmitriy A. Katz, Dennis Wei, Prasanna Sattigeri, and Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: For a single DAG under perfect interventions, interventional Markov equivalence has a graph-theoretic criterion and a unique interventional essential-graph representative.
source_refs.author: Alain Hauser and Peter Bühlmann

source_refs.claim: Single-DAG interventional equivalence and consistent structure learning extend beyond perfect interventions to general interventions.
source_refs.author: Karren Yang, Abigail Katcoff, and Caroline Uhler

open_problems.why_unsolved: Single-DAG equivalence criteria rely on a shared skeleton and augmented-graph skeleton or v-structure information; these representations do not account for a latent component selector whose children create emergent inseparabilities across barred graph copies. Varıcı et al. characterize when one candidate edge can be exposed by a selected intervention and show that component partitions can remain indistinguishable under all targets, but local pairwise criteria do not determine when every conditional-independence answer agrees simultaneously. That missing global criterion is exactly what a legal adaptive transcript lower bound needs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if graphical criterion for size-s oracle equivalence of two K-DAG mixtures, together with a canonical partially oriented union object whose directed marks are exactly the union-edge orientations shared by the equivalence class.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates why ordinary observational equivalence is inadequate for mixtures and provides the local interventional separability and indistinguishability phenomena.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Mixtures add emergent pairs beyond true edges -> interventions refine but do not always eliminate ambiguity -> local parent tests do not organize all globally indistinguishable mixtures -> characterize mixture interventional oracle-equivalence classes.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the augmented-intervention-graph equivalence criterion and essential-graph uniqueness proof to I-mixture DAGs with barred node sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies precisely the requested kind of if-and-only-if equivalence theorem and canonical representative; the changed proof step is replacing ordinary skeleton and v-structure agreement by barred-copy separation agreement through the selector.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the mixture-DAG Markov representation and latent-projection arguments to determine which separation invariants survive marginalization over component identity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the observational mixture analogue of a graphical representation and connects encoded separation statements to recovery of a union object.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt joint observational-interventional likelihood scoring and its BIC-consistency proof after replacing single-DAG interventional equivalence classes by the mixture representative.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves consistent estimation of the structurally analogous single-DAG interventional-equivalence object and therefore supplies a concrete finite-sample rung for the new characterization.

open_problems.open_problem: Define a mixture-union verification number and characterize the r-round adaptivity hierarchy for size-at-most-s interventions, including whether bounded cyclic complexity tau permits a universal-factor search-to-verification reduction or an exponential adaptive advantage.

source_refs.claim: For single-DAG discovery, r-round algorithms have tight approximation guarantees relative to the verification number, with extensions to bounded-size interventions.
source_refs.author: Davin Choo and Kirankumar Shiragur

source_refs.claim: For one DAG, minimal verifying sets are characterized through covered-edge separation, and adaptive search is logarithmically competitive with verification.
source_refs.author: Davin Choo, Kirankumar Shiragur, and Arnab Bhattacharyya

source_refs.claim: Mixture discovery has O(n^2) adaptive intervention complexity and a tau-controlled intervention-size gap, but no verification benchmark or adaptivity-round tradeoff.
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Dmitriy A. Katz, Dennis Wei, Prasanna Sattigeri, and Ali Tajer

open_problems.why_unsolved: This direction transfers single-DAG verification and adaptivity machinery to mixture-union recovery. The donor proof first reduces verification to hitting covered edges of a fixed DAG inside a known MEC. That step fails for mixtures because the target is a union, observational data need not reveal its skeleton, and a proposed true edge must be verified against emergent-nonedge alternatives whose blocker sets can conflict across components. The mixture paper supplies no replacement benchmark and only bounds total interventions by O(n^2); the searched literature contains r-adaptivity and verification theorems for single DAGs but no counterpart involving I-mixture DAGs, cyclic complexity, and union-edge recovery.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A definition of nu_s^mix for mixture-union verification and matching upper and lower r-round search bounds in terms of nu_s^mix,n,K,tau, or a counterexample family ruling out such a reduction, instantiated with an explicit adaptive policy and legal indistinguishable transcripts.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation turns limits on sequential experimentation into a clean r-round minimax hierarchy.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nonadaptive designs can be much more expensive than fully adaptive ones -> practical experimentation permits limited feedback rounds -> verification supplies a common lower benchmark -> determine the r-round hierarchy for mixture-union recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace the covered-edge characterization by a hitting problem over minimal true-edge-versus-emergent mixture alternatives, then adapt the graph-separator charging argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is a direct mixture analogue of verification versus search; the structural task is to identify the correct minimal alternatives and prove that their blockers can be amortized.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt balanced partitioning and the round-elimination lower-bound construction, replacing essential-graph chain components by unresolved mixture alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives tight r-round tradeoffs under bounded intervention size in the nearest existing oracle model.

method_exemplars.technique: Use adaptive allocation matching and track-and-stop confidence rules to obtain finite-sample, fixed-confidence recovery for alternatives exposed by the population verification theorem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It converts a separating intervention family into an adaptive finite-sample recovery procedure, which is the natural estimation rung after an oracle adaptivity theorem.

literature_map:
1. Saeed, Panigrahi, and Uhler (ICML 2020, arXiv:2001.11940) introduced a mixture-DAG representation, proved its Markov semantics, and recovered a union graph under poset compatibility.
2. Strobl (Machine Learning 2023) used mixtures of DAGs for longitudinal causal discovery, emphasizing time variation, latent variables, selection, and cross-regime cycles.
3. Varıcı et al. (TMLR 2024) characterized observational separability and emergent edges; cyclic cross-component paths obstruct simpler poset-compatible union reasoning.
4. Varıcı, Katz, Wei, Sattigeri, and Tajer (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2406.08666) introduced I-mixture DAGs and I-mixture faithfulness, established local intervention-size thresholds, and gave CADIM.
5. That paper's explicit unresolved boundary is the number of constrained-size interventions: CADIM uses O(n^2), while matching count lower bounds are left for future work.
6. Hauser and Bühlmann (JMLR 2012, arXiv:1104.2808) characterized perfect-intervention Markov equivalence and unique interventional essential graphs for one DAG.
7. Yang, Katcoff, and Uhler (ICML 2018, arXiv:1802.06310) extended single-DAG equivalence and consistent learning to general interventions; no global mixture counterpart was found.
8. Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer (JMLR 2013) connected single-system experiment selection to separating systems and exact combinatorial designs.
9. Shanmugam, Kocaoglu, Dimakis, and Vishwanath (NeurIPS 2015, arXiv:1511.00041) proved bounded-size separating-system necessity against adaptivity on complete skeletons and broader information-theoretic lower bounds.
10. Lindgren, Kocaoglu, Dimakis, and Vishwanath (NeurIPS 2018, arXiv:1810.11867) derived sparse separating-system bounds and near-optimal nonadaptive designs for sparse chordal graphs.
11. Greenewald et al. (NeurIPS 2019) gave a factor-two central-node policy for one causal tree and showed information-greedy selection can be exponentially suboptimal; mixtures break its unique-root progress argument.
12. Squires et al. (NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2011.00641) and Porwal, Srivastava, and Sinha (AISTATS 2022, arXiv:2111.05070) developed single-DAG lower bounds using directed clique trees and causal orderings.
13. Choo, Shiragur, and Bhattacharyya (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2206.15374) characterized verification through covered-edge separation and obtained adaptive search guarantees, but this reduction has no known mixture analogue.
14. Choo and Shiragur (UAI 2023, arXiv:2306.05781) established tight r-round adaptivity tradeoffs, including bounded-size interventions; no I-mixture adaptivity hierarchy was found.
15. Mokhtarian, Salehkaleybar, Ghassami, and Kiyavash (JMLR 2023, arXiv:2205.10083) treated experiment design for cyclic SCMs, whereas mixture-ancestor cycles are selector-induced obstructions among individually acyclic components.
